video_title: A Massive Coaching Drama + Could Kawhi Be Traded? & Can Pistons Get Cade Help?

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Coaches are upset about the structure of Micah Nori's contract
quotes.excerpt: I talked to several coaches who were absolutely irate about the circumstances, specifically the structure of this contract.
quotes.quote: Everybody in the coaching community loves Micah Nori and respects Micah Nori and thinks that he is ready and deserving of a head coaching job. I talked to several coaches who were absolutely irate about the circumstances, specifically the structure of this contract. This is Tom Dunden's work. This is that Stanley Cup winning, Dallas-based billionaire who, in his brief time in the NBA, has been notoriously cheap, frugal, doesn't travel two-way guys for the playoffs, has had layoffs, no late checkout. That's how he conducted this coaching search, which by the way, started midway through the season while Thiago Splitter was working his ass off under insane circumstances leading your team to the playoffs, and you're interviewing mid-major coaches who are telling you, 'Dude, I make more money than what you're talking about offering.'

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori accepted a contract as a 'renter coach' on probation
quotes.excerpt: Micah Nori accepted a contract as a renter coach. It's a one plus one plus one contract.
quotes.quote: Micah Nori accepted a contract as a renter coach. It's a one plus one plus one contract. It's a three-year deal with team options for the second and third year. I heard from a whole lot of coaches, a few were ready to go on the record and backed out. Props to JB Bickerstaff, who is the president of the NBCA, the National Basketball Coaches Association. He felt like it was his duty as the president of that organization to take a firm stance on this. He felt like this contract was a slap in the face to our value.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Tom Dunden claimed the Blazers spend $100 million more than the Hurricanes
quotes.excerpt: Tom Dunden came out and said that the Blazers spend $100 million more than the Carolina Hurricanes do.
quotes.quote: If you're Tom Dunden, he came out and said that the Blazers spend $100 million more than the Carolina Hurricanes do. He basically is like, that can't be right. And so, and by the way, I am not his advocate. I am not arguing for him. I do not have his side. I am trying to just be fair. He didn't kick the players out of the hotel. He kicked some staff members out of the hotel early and didn't give them a late checkout. And it was a hotel in San Antonio that it was a one-off situation. It's not all road trips.

quotes.speaker: Vince Goodwill
quotes.summary_phrase: The Blazers' treatment of staff sets a terrible precedent
quotes.excerpt: It sets a terrible precedent. You put Micah Nori in a completely unfair situation.
quotes.quote: It sets a terrible precedent. You put Micah Nori in a completely unfair situation. Like Joe Mazzulla and Mitch Johnson were guys who were in the building. Adverse situation when you talk about Ime Udoka and his situation and Gregg Popovich having a stroke. Those guys were in the building and then you take over on an interim basis and you figure out the rest later. They had Thiago Splitter in the building this year. Thiago Splitter on the second day of the damn season had to slide in when Chauncey Billups was indicted and everything else and he took that team to the playoffs. That team not only stayed together but got better throughout the course of the year and leapfrogged a bunch of teams that we thought were better from a talent standpoint and you let him walk to the Portland Trail Blazers.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Austin Reaves' contract was a fascinating situation of leverage
quotes.excerpt: I do think the Austin Reaves contract, what we saw, was a fascinating situation of leverage.
quotes.quote: I do think the Austin Reaves contract, what we saw, was a fascinating situation of leverage. The Lakers, from my knowledge, he signed a four years, 185. From what I was told, the Lakers were in the range of five years, 150 for Austin Reaves a couple of days ago. 30 million dollars a year. Very good contract, significantly higher than what he was making right now. And I'm, I mean, it wasn't their final offer, clearly, but that's where they were in the range of. And some teams in the league who thought they might have a shot at Austin were like, 'Wow, if that's where they're at, we might be able to get him.'

quotes.speaker: Vince Goodwill
quotes.summary_phrase: Detroit needs to get Cade Cunningham a co-star
quotes.excerpt: You have your star now in Cade Cunningham. Do you still have the appetite to go get a co-star?
quotes.quote: The crazy thing is the stuff that you heard over the past couple of days before now, you heard about Austin Reaves, you heard about Kobe White. Both of those guys are signed. Now you have all this money and I take people back, because we're talking about ownership. Tom Goris is an LA guy and he was the guy who spearheaded that Blake Griffin deal all those years ago, six months after Blake Griffin signed that deal with the Clippers. And he got his star and they learned a lot of lessons in how to build a team. You have your star now in Cade Cunningham. Do you still have the appetite to go get a co-star? I mean, look, when you trade Isaiah Stewart, who makes 15 million dollars a year, who's arguably the best rim protector this side of Victor Wembanyama and a big piece of that culture, you trade him for peanuts, you'd better have a plan.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Kawhi Leonard's contract situation is a major offseason question
quotes.excerpt: I wish I could tell you I knew what's going to happen here. I don't.
quotes.quote: I wish I could tell you I knew what's going to happen here. I don't, and a lot of the league doesn't. He's coming off a season. He played in 65 games, so he was able to make all-NBA. He averaged 28 points. That was the most points of any season in his career. Shot 51% from the field and was an absolute beast from that mid-range that we saw, back to like his peak of his career really, from that mid-range. One-year contract at $50 million. Not necessarily in position to be getting a four-year max here, but definitely looking like he could get another contract. And certainly the way he's playing, you would extend that guy. You would either extend that guy or you would trade him. The last thing you would do is have him on an expiring contract.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers have three players with team options to decide on
quotes.excerpt: They got three guys, Brook Lopez, Bogdan Bogdanovic, Nicolas Batum, all of them on team options.
quotes.quote: They got three guys, Brook Lopez, Bogdan Bogdanovic, Nicolas Batum, all of them on team options. They don't owe money to any of them. They got to make a decision by this weekend. They cut all of them, that shaves $53 million off. They could be a cap space team. Obviously, they could keep them and run back with Kawhi. By the way, Steve Ballmer has never indicated he wants to like go down. Like I think Steve Ballmer, his investment in Kawhi is so deep, I don't see it stopping. But also, Kawhi has, if he's, if he's allowed to be traded and he's not going to face a significant suspension, if he's, you know, either gets a light penalty or none at all, he's got immense, he's got more value right now than he's had in years.
